findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: 9 February 1913: The first assault of the Decena Trágica took place in the Zócalo, against the National Palace; General Lauro Villar's loyalist forces regained the palace after insurgents initially entered it.
evidence_locators: UNAM Filmoteca chronology, paragraphs on 9 February
findings.uncertainty: Supported in two institutional narratives; original military records unexamined
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: The Library of Congress exhibition states that 232 captured troops from the Military Aspirants School were held in the Metropolitan Cathedral for two days after the failed 9 February assault; the exact number and confinement require independent documentary corroboration.
findings.uncertainty: Single curated exhibition assertion; original arrest rolls unexamined
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: Bernardo Reyes was killed during the 9 February attack on the National Palace; the insurgents subsequently consolidated at the Ciudadela arsenal rather than occupying the Palace.
evidence_locators: LOC Madero presidency, section Tragic Ten Days
findings.uncertainty: Convergent secondary historical syntheses; precise tactical details still provisional
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: The 11 February fighting extended to Calle Balderas between the Ciudadela and the former YMCA building, where the Library of Congress map describes machine-gun fire against loyalist troops.
findings.uncertainty: Single exhibition reconstruction; weapon positions require primary/photographic checks
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: The Library of Congress situates Madero's 9 February return from Chapultepec via Avenida Juárez toward the National Palace; this allows a historically grounded route narrative but the route's precise stops should not be asserted without primary evidence.
findings.uncertainty: Curated exhibition; exact street itinerary not independently verified
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: On 18 February 1913 Victoriano Huerta and Félix Díaz reached an agreement brokered through US ambassador Henry Lane Wilson, known as the Pacto de la Ciudadela or Pacto de la Embajada, during the overthrow of Madero.
evidence_locators: UNAM Filmoteca chronology, final coup paragraph
findings.uncertainty: Multiple institutional summaries; original treaty/signatures unexamined
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: The Library of Congress interactive chronology places Madero's 19 February resignation negotiations in the National Palace's administrative rooms and reports four conditions, including protections for state governments and a safe departure to Veracruz.
findings.uncertainty: Exhibition account; original resignation document not inspected
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: The broader 1913 coup sequence should not be collapsed into the 'Decena Trágica' fighting period: the revolt started on 9 February, the overthrow proceeded on 18–19 February, and Madero and Pino Suárez were assassinated on 22 February.
evidence_locators: LOC interactive map, introductory paragraph and Eventos Dieciocho–Veinticuatro
UNAM Filmoteca chronology, introductory and closing paragraphs
LOC Madero presidency, section Tragic Ten Days
findings.uncertainty: Chronology correction; historical event start/end terminology varies
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: The Filmoteca UNAM identifies approximately thirty minutes of surviving film material related to the Decena Trágica in the Salvador Toscano collection, including contemporary footage credited to Guillermo Becerril, Enrique Echániz and Hermanos Alva.
evidence_locators: UNAM Filmoteca chronology, archival note and list of films
findings.uncertainty: Institutional collection description; footage and reproduction rights not inspected
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

findings.subject: Decena Trágica and 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: The Library of Congress map places the murders of Francisco I. Madero and José María Pino Suárez on 22 February 1913 behind the Federal District penitentiary, distinct in time and location from the 9 February Zócalo fighting.
evidence_locators: LOC Madero presidency, section Tragic Ten Days
findings.uncertainty: Museum account; original case and autopsy records unexamined
findings.educational_use: National Palace / Zócalo 1913 map-based walk with evidence-linked contextual deep dive

conflicting_legacy_records.issue: Date range is not the standard ten-day fighting interval and may conflate the 22 February murders and later aftermath with the core Decena Trágica; do not overwrite original
conflicting_legacy_records.recommended_action: human editorial review, separate 9–18 fighting, 18–19 coup, 22 February murders

conflicting_legacy_records.issue: LOC Evento Diecinueve places 18 February arrest at Restaurante Gambrinus, whereas UNAM general account and other histories place Madero's arrest at Palacio Nacional
conflicting_legacy_records.recommended_action: Do not assert the exact arrest room without manuscript or corroborated documentation

conflicting_legacy_records.issue: The LOC places Gustavo Madero's violent death in its 19 February event, whereas other institutional accounts date it to the night of 18 February
conflicting_legacy_records.recommended_action: Verify original dated records before precise date publication

evidence_limit: None of the primary military dispatches, presidential resignation originals, court/autopsy files, or archival film frames were inspected. No licensed image rights acquired.
